newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmiris pray for peace as crucial polls resume.
newsitem.headline: Kashmiris pray for peace as crucial polls resume.

text.p: Moslems in Kashmir prayed for peace on Monday as they braced for the second phase of local elections in which campaign violence has killed 20 people so far.

These are the first local polls since 1987. The assembly which emerged from those elections was dissolved in 1990 when the federal government clamped the state under direct rule in an effort to quell a separatist revolt.

Shopkeepers across the region planned a second day of closures on Monday, after separatist leaders asked them to join a three-week old strike involving schools, banks and government offices against the polls which they say are farcical.
"May the Almighty God bring peace to his miserable followers and end their suffering soon," a prayer leader in the state's summer capital of Srinagar said.
Loudhailers across the city echoed similar prayers.
Most leading separatist groups have urged voters to boycott the polls, viewed as crucial to Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's efforts to restore democracy in the state.
Dozens of militant groups are fighting for independence or merger with Pakistan, which rules one third of Kashmir, called Azad (Free) Kashmir.

Nearly 50 years after India and Pakistan gained independence from Britain, Kashmir remains the biggest obstacle to closer ties between Islamabad and New Delhi. They have fought two of three wars since independence over the region.
Indian security officials said they were optimistic about voting in the 34 constituencies for the 87-seat Jammu and Kashmir state assembly on Monday.
"We expect the 34 elections today to be even better than the first phase," a police official told Reuters in the state's summer capital of Srinagar.
But officials said they expected tension in the districts of Anantnag and Pulwama, south of Srinagar, which they said were traditional strongholds of Moslem militants.
On September 7, voters cast ballots in 26 constituencies. Officials said 53 percent voters had cast their ballot that day.
Voting in the remaining constituencies is scheduled for September 21 and 30.
Fear of violence during the elections has forced some supporters of politicians to wear masks. More than 20,000 people have been killed since the outbreak of the rebellion in 1990.
"The fact that political supporters are forced to wear masks does suggest an element of fear," a defence spokesman told Reuters on Sunday. "But their percentage is low.
Separatist politicians opposing the polls accuse the government of intimidating people to cast their votes.

"An election in which political supporters wear masks and people are coerced to cast their vote with all kinds of threats is a laughable way to solve Kashmir's problems," Professor Abdul Ghani, a spokesman for the separatist Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference, told Reuters.
Indian officials called the first phase of the elections a peaceful triumph of democracy over militancy.
